claim_text: Whey protein is derived from milk and is not an appropriate default protein supplement for people with confirmed cow's milk protein allergy; lactose-free labeling does not establish absence of milk proteins.
health_goal_or_outcome: Prevent exposure to milk-derived whey in people with milk-protein allergy.

population.age_range: All ages; allergy severity and management differ.
population.health_status: People with confirmed or suspected cow's milk protein allergy.
population.other_context: Check full ingredient list and allergen labeling of the specific product.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Whey concentrate, isolate and hydrolysate; residual allergenic protein and product processing vary.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance fact sheet identifies whey as a milk-derived protein source; allergen-specific decisions require product label and allergy guidance.
limitations: Lactose intolerance is distinct from milk-protein allergy.
Hydrolysis does not automatically guarantee safety for every allergic individual.
Use allergist/clinician guidance for confirmed allergy.
